title: Nearest Hospital Finder: Closest Hospitals
description: Find the nearest hospitals to a place or your location with the Nearest Hospital Finder — mapped from open data, ranked by distance. Free.
summary_sentence: Results are limited to returned OpenStreetMap records and may omit closer or unmapped places. Confirm details with an authoritative local source.
quick_answer: The tool searches OpenStreetMap for mapped hospital records around a chosen location, then sorts returned records by straight-line distance. It requests at most 200 records and displays up to 100, so it cannot guarantee the closest result or a complete list. Data, access and opening status can be incomplete or outdated. In an emergency, contact local emergency services; this is not an emergency directory.

Distance to a hospital shapes real decisions about where ageing parents live. This makes the distance a number instead of an anxiety.
Use an official health directory and emergency plan to identify appropriate facilities. This capped list cannot establish which hospital is nearest or confirm its services.
Returned hospital records are sorted by straight-line distance. They may omit closer hospitals and do not confirm emergency care, opening status or road access.

If someone is seriously ill or injured now, call the emergency number (911 in the US, 999 in the UK, 112 across Europe) before opening any map. Ambulances navigate professionally; this finder informs people.

faq: Should I use this in an emergency?
Call your local emergency number first — 911, 999 or 112. Dispatchers send help and guide you. This finder is for preparation and orientation, and says so at the top of the page.
Why might a hospital be missing?
It may be unrecorded in OpenStreetMap, newly built, or recorded as a clinic rather than a hospital. Coverage is strong in towns and cities; remote areas are thinner — the pattern of all open data.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
You can search for a place instead of using device location. The selected search centre is sent to OpenStreetMap-based services for the lookup.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Hospital names change with trusts and systems; official directories are the freshest name source.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
Device location is optional. The selected coordinates are sent to Overpass to search; consult the privacy page for provider and site details.
Does it show emergency departments?
No. Hospital records are not checked for emergency department services or current operating status; verify with an official health directory.
Straight-line distance misleads across water or mountains.
True of every ranking on earth — the list order is the starting point; your route app refines the drive. Knowing the candidates is the step this page owns.
Clinics and urgent care?
The query selects records tagged amenity=hospital, not clinics as a separate category. Check official healthcare directories.
Outside the US and Europe?
The finder works wherever OpenStreetMap has hospital records — which is most of the populated world, at varying depth.
Children's hospitals?
Some named hospital records may indicate a specialty, but this tool does not verify services. Check an official health directory.
Urgent care centres?
The query selects hospital-tagged records and does not verify urgent care services. Use an official directory and contact emergency services if needed.
